children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child. 

**To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I first need to know about the child's age:**

Is your child:
- **Under 16 years old**
- **Between 16-19 years old**, or
- **20 years old or over**?

This is important because the age of the child affects the basic eligibility criteria. Children under 16 generally qualify automatically (subject to other conditions), while those aged 16-19 may still qualify if they're in approved education or training.

Please let me know your child's age category, and if you have multiple children, we can assess each one.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 8 years old, so definitely under 16.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you! Since Alex is 8 years old, he's under 16, so let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now, the next question:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

Since Alex is only 8 years old, he almost certainly isn't working, but I need to confirm this as part of the eligibility check. Children who work 24 or more hours per week and aren't in approved education or training would not be eligible.

Can you confirm that Alex is not in paid work or works less than 24 hours per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's only 8, so he's just at school like any other child his age.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent, that's what I expected! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

Specifically, I'm asking whether Alex receives Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in his own name. Most children, especially at age 8, don't receive these benefits themselves, so this typically applies to older children.

Can you confirm that Alex is not receiving ESA or Universal Credit in his own right?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Next question:

**Is Alex NOT in a disqualifying apprenticeship?**

This question is about whether Alex is enrolled in certain types of apprenticeships that would disqualify him from Child Benefit. Given that Alex is only 8 years old and in regular school, he's not in any apprenticeship program.

Can you confirm that Alex is not in any apprenticeship program? (This is just a standard check - apprenticeships are for much older young people!)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. Like I said, he's only 8 and just goes to primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Absolutely, that makes perfect sense! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we need to check your residency status. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You can qualify through ANY of these paths:

1. **You normally live in the UK**, or
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or
3. You have pre-settled status and meet certain conditions (working, studying, actively seeking work, having sufficient resources, or being a family member of an EEA/Swiss national), or
4. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

Most people qualify simply by normally living in the UK. 

**Do you normally live in the UK?** Or do any of the other special circumstances apply to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm based here with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You qualify as being responsible if ANY of these apply:

1. **You live with Alex**, or
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep by paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards his care - this includes food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, or
3. You pay maintenance for Alex under a court order or agreement that equals or exceeds the Child Benefit amount

Since you mentioned you're based in the UK with Alex, it sounds like you live with him. **Can you confirm that you live with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check an important question about other potential claimants.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child at a time. For example:
- If you and Alex's other parent are separated, is the other parent claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Is anyone else (like a grandparent or other family member) claiming for Alex?

Please let me know:
- **No one else is claiming** for Alex, or
- **Someone else is claiming** but you've agreed they will transfer it to you, or
- **Someone else is claiming** and there's a dispute about who should claim

What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check where Alex is currently living, as there are special rules for certain situations.

**Which of these best describes Alex's living situation?**

- **Living normally at home with you** (standard situation)
- **Currently in hospital** (for an extended period)
- **In local authority care** (placed by the council)
- **In foster care**

Since you mentioned Alex lives at home with you and goes to primary school, I expect he's living normally at home. Can you confirm this is the case?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. Alex lives normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, care, or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Just one final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, the local council is not contributing financially towards Alex's living costs or care. Since Alex lives at home with you in a normal family situation, this almost certainly doesn't apply.

Can you confirm that the local council is not paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct. The council isn't paying anything towards Alex. He just lives with me as a normal family situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me process this final information.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You're ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!

Based on the information you've provided, **you meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex is a qualifying child** - He's 8 years old (under 16)  
✅ **Not working** - Alex is not in paid employment  
✅ **Not receiving benefits** - Alex doesn't receive ESA or Universal Credit in his own right  
✅ **Not in an apprenticeship** - Alex is in regular primary school  
✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You normally live in the UK  
✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - You live with him and care for him  
✅ **No competing claims** - No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex  
✅ **Normal living situation** - Alex lives at home with you  
✅ **No local authority support** - The council isn't paying for Alex's care  

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earn over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay some or all of the benefit back through tax
5. **Payments** are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

You can apply here: [https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)

Do you have any questions about the application process or anything else?

All eligibility criteria are met.
